summary: Decompose R FactoMineR GPA.R (860 lines) into an implementable spec: algorithm, output structure, fixture+test strategy

algo.overview:
GPA.R (lines 1-860) implements FactoMineR's Generalized Procrustes Analysis. It takes a single data.frame `df` whose columns are the horizontal concatenation of K configurations (one per "judge"/group), plus an integer vector `group` giving the column-count of each configuration. It optimally rotates (orthogonal), reflects, isotropically scales, and translates the K configurations onto a common consensus, then returns the consensus, transformed configs (Xfin), scaling weights, and inter-configuration similarity matrices (RV, RVs, simi) plus a PANOVA decomposition.

Top-level flow (lines 727-859):
1. Default name.group = "group.1".."group.K" (727-728); validate df is a data.frame (729-730).
2. Build a 3D array X of shape (nrow(df), max(group), K), padding configs with fewer columns by zeros (733-742). Xdd = raw X (743), used later for RV/simi.
3. X1 <- calibre(X) (745): per-config PCA pre-rotation onto principal axes (scale.unit=FALSE), unequal dims padded with zero columns, NA rows preserved.
4. gpafin <- algogpa(X1, ...) (747): the core iterative Procrustes engine. NOTE the top-level call uses algogpa's DEFAULT tolerance=1e-7 and nbiteration=200, NOT the GPA() argument tolerance (the GPA-level tolerance/nbiteration are only threaded into f1ter). 
5. gpares <- f1ter(X1, P=5, ...) (749-750): runs algogpa P=5 more times on randomly permuted/sign-flipped/column-permuted copies, picks the run with the smallest residual crit() (the multi-start to escape local optima). The chosen run's arrays are de-permuted back to original config order via `odd <- order(permutab)` (751-760).
6. Recompute Xdep = calibre(X) for display (761-763).
7. Assemble RV / RVs / simi K x K matrices from raw Xdd (765-812), with a missing-value branch (VMQTE) that drops rows missing in either config (768-800) vs the clean branch (802-811).
8. Build per-config correlations of centered raw columns with consensus (816-837); only add an "averagecor" if all configs have the same #columns (827).
9. Mask Xfin rows that were missing back to NA if VMQTE (839-843).
10. Return list of class "GPA": RV, RVs, simi, scaling, dep, consensus, Xfin, correlations, PANOVA (844-859).
algo.preprocessing:
Splitting (lines 731-742): `blo <- group`; `nbjuge <- length(group)` = K. X is array(0, c(nrow(df), max(blo), K)). A running `indice` walks the columns of df; config i takes columns (indice+1):(indice+blo[i]) and is placed into X[, 1:blo[i], i], leaving columns blo[i]+1..max(blo) as zeros (the zero-padding for unequal dims). So configs are contiguous column blocks of df in order.

calibre() pre-rotation (lines 687-726): each config X[,,i] is replaced by its PCA individual coordinates with scale.unit=FALSE (i.e. column-centered, NOT unit-variance scaled), ncp=min(nrow,ncol). This is a per-config rotation to principal axes / column-centering done BEFORE algogpa. Configs with NA rows (placevm finds rows containing any NA, lines 231-252) run PCA on the non-missing rows then re-insert results with NA rows preserved (701-723). All configs are re-padded to max(dimlist) columns with zeros (711-714). So the matrices entering algogpa are already centered.

scale=TRUE per-config NORMALIZATION happens inside algogpa, in two stages:
(a) Global normalization to total weighted sum-of-squares = nbjuge: lambda2 = sum over j of trace(t(Xm1[,,j]) Cj[,,j] Xm1[,,j]) (lines 367-371); lambda = (nbjuge/lambda2)^0.5 (372); Xnorm = Xm1 * lambda (373) — a single common scalar applied to ALL configs so the grand weighted SS equals K.
(b) W12 = diag( 1 / sqrt(trace(t(Xnorm[,,i]) Cj[,,i] Xnorm[,,i])) ) per config (lines 374-379), a diagonal of inverse per-config Procrustes norms used inside the scaling-weight eigen-step. Cj is the centering operator built from the missing-data mask M (see procrustes_step). Note Xm1 first replaces NA with 999999 (lines 361-366) but those rows are zeroed out by M/Cj so they do not contribute.
algo.procrustes_step:
Core helper procrustesbis(X1, X2) (lines 253-311) computes the orthogonal matrix H rotating X1 toward X2 (both column-centered first: X1c=scale(X1,scale=FALSE), X2c=scale(X2,scale=FALSE), lines 261-262). Cross-product Aj = t(X1c) %*% X2c (263). It does NOT use a direct SVD of Aj; instead it eigendecomposes t(Aj) %*% Aj: lola = eigen(t(Aj)%*%Aj), Qj = eigenvectors, phij = diag(eigenvalues) (264-266). Rank via opp1 = sqrt(|eigenvalues|), rang = number of opp1/opp1[1] > 1e-7 (267-269).

Full-rank branch (rang == length, lines 276-280): Pj = Aj %*% Qj %*% diag(diag(phij)^(-0.5)); H = Pj %*% t(Qj). This is algebraically the orthogonal polar factor of Aj = U V^T from SVD Aj = U D V^T (since Qj=V, Aj Qj phij^{-1/2} = U). So H is the orthogonal Procrustes rotation. REFLECTIONS ARE ALLOWED — H is a general orthogonal matrix (det can be -1), there is no det>0 / determinant-correction restriction to pure rotation. A Python port should use scipy SVD of Aj: U,_,Vt = svd(Aj); H = U @ Vt (NOT orthogonal_procrustes' R = Vt.T@U.T convention — note R is the transpose, so map carefully). 

Rank-deficient branch (rang < length, lines 281-303): builds Pjstar from the leading rang eigenvectors, then completes the orthonormal basis Pbar by orthogonalizing random Gaussian vectors (rnorm) against Pjstar via lm regression residuals (288-301), with a sign alignment to Qj columns. H = Pjstar1 %*% t(lola$vectors) (302). This RANDOMIZED completion is a porting trap (see gotchas). 

rho (isotropic scale of this single pairwise fit, line 304-305): rho = trace(X1c %*% H %*% t(X2c)) / trace(X1c %*% t(X1)). In the main GPA loop only $H is used (R[,,j] = procrustesbis(...)$H, lines 394-396, 457-459); rho from procrustesbis is NOT the per-config scaling weight — that comes from the W12 eigen-step. procrustesbis is also used by similarite (line 25).
algo.iteration_loop:
Setup (lines 380-446): pds (the per-config scaling weights "poids") initialized to rep(1, K) (380); R[,,i] (rotations) initialized to identity Im (381-385). 

Pre-loop rotation pass (lines 387-397): for each j, sommetemp = sum over all i of pds[i]*Cj[,,i] %*% Xnorm[,,i] %*% R[,,i]; then R[,,j] = procrustesbis( Cj[,,j] %*% Xnorm[,,j],  invgC %*% (sommetemp - pds[j]*Cj[,,j] %*% Xnorm[,,j] %*% R[,,j]) )$H. So each config is rotated toward the leave-one-out consensus invgC %*% (sum of the OTHER configs), where invgC = ginv(Cc), Cc = sum of Cj (355-359). This is sequential (Gauss-Seidel style: updated R[,,j] feeds the next j's sommetemp).

Initial loss (lines 398-408): consensus accumulator sommetemp2 = sum pds[i]*Cj[,,i]Xnorm[,,i]R[,,i]; lossf = nbjuge - trace(t(sommetemp2) %*% invgC %*% sommetemp2). If scale, an initial scaling-weight eigen-step (lines 409-442) recomputes pds and lossf2 (see scaling_factors).

Main while loop (lines 449-511): condition `tol > tolerance && compteur < nbiteration` with tolerance=1e-7 (algogpa default; the f1ter runs pass the GPA-level tolerance=1e-10) and nbiteration=200. Each iteration:
1. Rotation sub-step (450-460): same sequential per-config R[,,j] = procrustesbis(...)$H update as the pre-loop pass, against the leave-one-out consensus.
2. Recompute sommetemp2 and lossf2ortho = nbjuge - trace(t(sommetemp2) invgC sommetemp2) (461-471).
3. If scale: scaling sub-step recomputes pds via the W12 eigen step and updates lossf2 (472-504).
4. Convergence: tol = (lossf - lossf2); lossf = lossf2 (506-507); record itorth/itpoids (508-509); compteur++ (510). 
So convergence is on the DECREASE in the loss between iterations (tol = previous loss - current loss), stopping when the improvement falls below tolerance or after 200 iterations. lossf/lossf2 are the residual loss = K - trace(Z' Cc Z)-style quantity.
algo.scaling_factors:
The per-config isotropic scaling weights are `pds` (returned as x$poids, exposed as result$scaling, line 849). They are computed only when scale=TRUE, via an eigenvector step, both pre-loop (lines 409-442) and inside each iteration (472-504), identically:
1. B[,,k] = Cj[,,k] %*% Xnorm[,,k] %*% R[,,k] for each k (rotated centered configs) (412-415 / 475-479).
2. matY[k,l] = trace( t(B[,,k]) %*% invgC %*% B[,,l] ) — a K x K Gram matrix of the rotated configs through the consensus metric invgC (416-421 / 480-485).
3. eigzou = eigen(W12 %*% matY %*% W12), where W12 = diag(1/sqrt(per-config Procrustes norm)) from lines 374-379 (422 / 486).
4. Take the FIRST (largest) eigenvector. Sign fix: if every entry of the first eigenvector is negative (sum(vec<0)==length), negate it so weights are positive (423-430 / 487-492).
5. pds = sqrt(nbjuge) * W12 %*% vecteurpropre (433 / 493). So the weights are the leading eigenvector of the symmetric matrix W12 matY W12, rescaled by W12 and normalized so that the total weighted SS stays = nbjuge.

These pds multiply each config everywhere consensus is formed: sommetemp = sum_i pds[i]*Cj[,,i] Xnorm[,,i] R[,,i] (e.g. 388-392, 451-455, 494-499), in the translation (522-524), and in the final Xfin (line 529: Xfin[,,k] = pds[k]*M[,,k]*(Xnorm[,,k]-U t(translation[,k])) R[,,k] K). When scale=FALSE, pds stays rep(1,K) throughout (no scaling). At the top level the final poids are de-permuted: gpafin$poids = as.matrix(x$poids[odd]) (line 760).
algo.consensus_and_xfin:
After the loop, the consensus point estimate pp = invgC %*% sommetemp2 (line 519) where sommetemp2 = sum_i pds[i]*Cj[,,i] Xnorm[,,i] R[,,i] (512-518). Translations per config: translation[,i] = ( t(pds[i]*Xnorm[,,i] - pp %*% t(R[,,i])) %*% M[,,i] %*% U ) / (pds[i]* t(U) M[,,i] U) (lines 520-525) — the weighted column means accounting for the missing-data mask M.

FINAL EIGEN-ROTATION (line 526): ppeig = eigen(t(pp) %*% Cc %*% pp) — eigendecomposition of the consensus' own (Cc-metric) cross-product. Its eigenvectors K_rot = ppeig$vectors rotate the consensus to its principal axes. 

Xfin (3D array N x dims x K, lines 527-531): for each config k, Xfin[,,k] = pds[k] * M[,,k] %*% (Xnorm[,,k] - U %*% t(translation[,k])) %*% R[,,k] %*% ppeig$vectors. I.e. scale by pds[k], mask missing rows (M), translate, rotate by R[,,k], then apply the common final eigen-rotation ppeig$vectors. 

consensus = pp %*% ppeig$vectors (line 535) — the consensus rotated to principal axes (this IS the final PCA/eigen rotation applied to the consensus). A trailing-zero-dimension trimmer (lines 536-548) finds `fina` = the last consensus column not effectively all-zero (|col| < sqrt(eps)), and the returned consensus = consensus[,1:fina] (564) and Xfin = Xfin[,1:fina,] (566) are truncated to fina columns. ppeig$values give result$gama = diag(ppeig$values) (573), the eigen-variances per consensus dimension. The result also stores Z=pp (565), Xdeb=Xnorm (567), Rj=R (571), K=ppeig$vectors (572). At the GPA top level, result$consensus = x$consensus and result$Xfin = Xfin (with VMQTE rows re-NA'd), lines 851-852.
algo.rv_and_similarity:
coeffRV(Xi, Xj) (lines 796-797, 807-808) is NOT defined in GPA.R — it is the external FactoMineR function coeffRV, which a Python port must reimplement. Standard FactoMineR definitions: given X, Y (each centered), let W1 = X %*% t(X), W2 = Y %*% t(Y). RV = trace(W1 %*% W2) / sqrt( trace(W1%*%W1) * trace(W2%*%W2) ) (this is the $rv field). The standardized RV ($rvstd) follows Smilde et al.: subtract the diagonals of W1 and W2 before forming the trace ratio — RVstd = trace(W1tilde %*% W2tilde)/sqrt(trace(W1tilde^2)*trace(W2tilde^2)) where Witilde = Wi with its diagonal set to zero (FactoMineR's coeffRV centers X,Y, then computes both rv and the bias-corrected rvstd). Port must match FactoMineR's coeffRV source exactly for tight tolerance. The matrices are filled symmetrically: RV[i,j]=RV[j,i], RVs[i,j]=RVs[j,i] over i<=j (776-799 / 803-811), initialized to -1 (765-767), row/col names = name.group (813-814).

similarite(X, Y) (lines 20-29): centers Y and X (scale=FALSE, lines 23-24); y = Y %*% procrustesbis(Y, X)$H (rotate Y onto X using H, line 25); then similari = trace(t(X) %*% y) / ( trace(t(X)%*%X) * trace(t(y)%*%y) )^0.5 (26-27). This is a Procrustes-rotation-based cosine/congruence between config X and rotated config Y. Result stored symmetrically in sim (798/809), names = name.group (815), exposed as result$simi (848).

Inputs to all three are the RAW per-config matrices Xdd[,,i] (the original pre-calibre array, line 743), NOT the calibre/PCA-rotated X1 — important: similarity is on raw data. The VMQTE branch (768-800) first drops rows that are missing in EITHER config i or j before calling the three functions.
gotchas: Reflections ARE allowed: procrustesbis returns a general orthogonal H (det can be -1) via H = U%*%Vt of Aj's SVD. Do NOT use scipy.linalg.orthogonal_procrustes naively — it returns R = Vt.T @ U.T (the transpose of what's used here as H = Pj%*%t(Qj) = U%*%Vt). Compute SVD of Aj directly and use U@Vt, and apply X1 %*% H (right-multiply), matching y = Y %*% H in similarite.

procrustesbis uses eigen(t(Aj)%*%Aj) not svd(Aj). For well-conditioned full-rank Aj this equals SVD, but eigen of A^T A squares the condition number — near-degenerate eigenvalues can flip eigenvector signs/order. Match R's eigen() ordering (descending eigenvalue) and the rank test rang = #{sqrt(|eig|)/sqrt(|eig|)[0] > 1e-7}.

Rank-deficient procrustesbis branch (lines 281-303) uses rnorm() random vectors + lm() to complete the orthonormal basis. This is NON-DETERMINISTIC and unseeded. A faithful port should instead complete the basis deterministically (e.g. via the null-space of Pjstar from a QR/SVD) — the random path only affects the rotation in the degenerate directions, which are projected out, but it WILL differ run-to-run in R. Document this divergence; for tight-tolerance matching, set R's seed or replace with deterministic completion in both.

Multi-start f1ter (lines 586-666) runs P=5 extra algogpa fits on randomly permuted configs (sample()), random column permutations, and random sign flips, then keeps the lowest-residual via crit() (577-585). This is unseeded randomness and can change which local optimum wins. To reproduce R exactly you must replicate R's RNG, or set.seed before GPA; otherwise consensus orientation/sign can differ. Note the de-permutation step `odd <- order(gpares$permutab)` reorders configs back (751-760).

Two different tolerances: GPA() default tolerance=1e-10 / nbiteration=200 are passed ONLY into f1ter's algogpa runs (line 749-750). The FIRST algogpa call (line 747) and algogpa's own signature use tolerance=1e-7 (line 312). Match this asymmetry.

Convergence criterion is tol = (lossf_prev - lossf_curr), the DECREASE in loss, not the loss magnitude (line 506). Stops when improvement < tolerance. Sign-flip / non-monotone loss could in principle make tol negative and stop early — preserve exact arithmetic.

Missing values (VMQTE): when any config row contains NA, M[,,j] is a diagonal mask zeroing those rows (lines 338-348), Cj uses M, and NA entries are replaced by 999999 in Xm1 (361-366) but zeroed by M/Cj. The clean path uses M=Ip and the simple centering Cj = Ip - (1/p) U U^T effectively. Port both paths; getting Cj = M(Ip - mat1 M / (U' M U)) right (lines 351-354) is essential — it's a weighted centering operator, not plain mean-subtraction, when masks differ.

Dimension padding: configs with fewer columns than max(group) are zero-padded both in the initial array (739) and in calibre (711-714). The trailing all-zero consensus columns are trimmed via `fina` (lines 536-548, 564, 566) — replicate the |col| < sqrt(eps) test exactly so output dim count matches.

Sign/orientation ambiguity: the consensus and Xfin are rotated by ppeig$vectors (eigen of t(pp)%*%Cc%*%pp, line 526). Eigenvector signs from eigen()/numpy.linalg.eig are arbitrary; also the W12 eigen-step (422/486) and the scaling-weight sign fix (only negates when ALL entries <0, lines 423-430/487-492) leave a global sign convention. Expect axis sign differences vs R unless you impose the same sign convention; compare up to per-axis sign and reflection.

calibre uses PCA(scale.unit=FALSE) — center-only, NOT standardize. The scale=TRUE argument of GPA controls the isotropic scaling-WEIGHT eigen-step (pds), it does NOT mean unit-variance scaling of columns. Don't conflate the two.

coeffRV is external (FactoMineR), not in this file — you must port FactoMineR::coeffRV separately for RV and rvstd; matching rvstd (the bias-corrected RV) requires the exact diagonal-correction formula, not the plain RV.

Indexing: R is 1-based and `for (i in 2:nbjuge)` assumes nbjuge>=2 (loops like 356-358, 390-392 will misbehave for K=1). Guard the K=1 case in Python (range(1,K) is empty, which is actually the correct behavior, but R's 2:1 produces c(2,1) — a real R bug for K=1). Most GPA use has K>=2.

result_fields.shape: K x K numpy array / DataFrame, row+col labels = name.group
result_fields.meaning: Escoufier RV coefficient between every pair of the K input configurations, computed on the calibrated (pre-Procrustes) data Xdd via coeffRV(Xi,Xj)$rv. Symmetric, diagonal = 1. Raw multivariate correlation between two configurations.

result_fields.shape: K x K numpy array / DataFrame, row+col labels = name.group
result_fields.meaning: Standardized/adjusted RV coefficient (coeffRV(Xi,Xj)$rvstd) between configuration pairs. The modified RV that corrects the upward bias of the raw RV in high dimensions. Symmetric.

result_fields.shape: K x K numpy array / DataFrame, row+col labels = name.group (R field name 'simi'; local var 'sim')
result_fields.meaning: Procrustes similarity index between configuration pairs: similarite(Xi,Xj) = sum(diag(t(X) %*% Y_rotated)) / sqrt(sum(diag(t(X)X)) * sum(diag(t(Y)Y))) after centering and optimal rotation of Y onto X. Symmetric; 1 = identical shapes.

result_fields.shape: length-K vector (in R a K x 1 matrix: as.matrix(x$poids[odd]))
result_fields.meaning: Per-configuration isotropic scaling weights (poids) found by GPA, reordered by the f1ter permutation. One scalar per input config; how much each config is stretched/shrunk onto the consensus.

result_fields.shape: In R nominally an N x maxdim x K 3D array (calibre(X) returns array(0, c(N, max(dimlist), K))); only dimnames[[1]] (rows = df rownames) and a 'dim j' colname vector are attached. Effectively the per-config starting coordinates.
result_fields.meaning: Xdep = calibre(X): the configurations after per-config PCA calibration but BEFORE Procrustes translation/rotation/scaling, i.e. the 'departure' state of the alignment. Auxiliary, mostly for plotting un-aligned configs.

result_fields.shape: N x D, row labels = df rownames, col labels 'dim 1..D'. D = number of retained consensus dimensions (fina), D <= max(dimlist) = width of the widest calibrated config.
result_fields.meaning: GPA consensus configuration: pp %*% ppeig$vectors truncated to the fina non-degenerate dimensions. The average aligned object positions; the primary low-dimensional map of individuals (analog of PCA ind$coord).

result_fields.shape: N x D x K 3D array (x$Xfin[,1:fina,]); rows = df rownames, K slabs over configurations. NA-filled at missing-value rows when VMQTE is TRUE.
result_fields.meaning: Each input configuration AFTER full Procrustes alignment (translation + rotation Rj + scaling poids + projection M) into the common consensus space. Slab i is config i in the same D-dim space as the consensus, so Xfin[:,:,i] - consensus is config i's residual. Primary per-config / partial-point output.

result_fields.shape: list/dict of length K (or K+1). Element i is a (blo[i] x D) matrix = cor(scale(Xdd[,1:blo[i],i]), consensus); named 'cor <name.group[i]>'. If all configs have equal width (max(blo)-blo[i] ~ 0 for all i) a final 'averagecor' element (same shape, elementwise mean) is appended, making length K+1.
result_fields.meaning: For each configuration, the Pearson correlation of its ORIGINAL (centered, un-calibrated) variables with each consensus dimension. Used to interpret what each consensus axis means in terms of the raw variables of each config (loading-style interpretation).

result_fields.shape: Named list/dict of DataFrames, NOT a single matrix; two branch variants. sansvm (no missing): keys objet ((N+1) x 3: SSfit/SSresidual/SStotal), config ((K+1) x 3), dimension ((D+1) x 3: Consensus/residus/Total), plus contribindivdim (N x 3D), contibis ((N+1) x 2K), contribconfigdim ((K+1) x 2D); all scaled /nbj*100. vmqte (missing-value branch): keys objet ((N+1) x 3), config ((K+1) x 3), dim ((D+1) x 3).
result_fields.meaning: Procrustes ANOVA: decomposition of total sum of squares into fit (consensus) vs residual, broken down per object, per configuration, and per dimension. The percentage-of-variance accounting tables. Auxiliary / diagnostic.

output.minimal_parity_set: Minimal meaningful parity set to assert for a first faithful port: consensus, Xfin, RV, RVs, simi, scaling, correlations. Rationale: consensus + Xfin are the core geometric outputs (consensus map and each aligned configuration); everything downstream/plotting derives from them. RV/RVs/simi are the headline inter-configuration agreement diagnostics users actually read, with stable well-defined K x K shapes that are easy to compare numerically against R. scaling (poids) is a tiny vector, cheap to verify, and a direct GPA solution output. correlations is needed to interpret axes and is a deterministic function of (Xdd, consensus). Treat PANOVA and dep as AUXILIARY for the first pass: PANOVA is a large, branch-dependent bundle of SS-decomposition tables that is laborious to reproduce exactly and is diagnostic rather than load-bearing; dep is the pre-alignment calibrated array used mostly for plotting and is even shape-ambiguous in R (3D array carrying 2D-style names). Important caveat: f1ter uses sample() (P=5 random restarts), so an EXACT numeric match to R is impossible without seeding. Parity should be asserted up to sign/rotation/permutation invariants (compare |RV|, similarity, consensus up to an orthogonal transform), or by seeding both sides. The port should expose a random_state argument like HCPC does.
output.result_container_mapping:
Recommend a dedicated GPAResult dataclass, NOT reuse of Result. Result is built around eig + svd + Block(coord/cos2/contrib/...) blocks indexed by ind/var/row/col; GPA produces none of these natively (no eigenvalue table, no SVD object, no per-variable coord/cos2 blocks). Three GPA fields are shapes the Block/Result model cannot hold: a 3D Xfin (N x D x K), three K x K agreement matrices, and a list/dict of ragged per-config correlation matrices. Forcing these into Block would misrepresent the data. HCPCResult (factominer/hcpc.py) is the established precedent for exactly this case: a frozen dataclass with method-specific fields (data_clust / desc_var / desc_axes / desc_ind / call) and a custom __repr__, not subclassing Result. Mirror it.

Concrete container design (add to a new factominer/gpa.py, keep frozen=True like HCPCResult):

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GPAResult:
    consensus: pd.DataFrame                       # N x D, index = row names, cols 'dim 1..D' (primary map)
    Xfin: np.ndarray                              # 3D N x D x K, aligned configs (NaN on missing rows)
    RV: pd.DataFrame                              # K x K, index/cols = name_group
    RVs: pd.DataFrame                             # K x K
    simi: pd.DataFrame                            # K x K
    scaling: pd.Series                            # length K, index = name_group (poids)
    correlations: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]         # 'cor <group>' -> (blo[i] x D); optional 'averagecor'
    PANOVA: dict[str, pd.DataFrame] = field(default_factory=dict)  # SS-decomposition tables (auxiliary)
    dep: np.ndarray | None = None                 # calibrated departure configs (auxiliary; 3D N x maxdim x K)
    call: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)            # group, name_group, K, D, scale, tolerance, random_state, VMQTE

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f\"<factominer.GPA configs={self.RV.shape[0]} dims={self.consensus.shape[1]}>\"

Design notes: (1) Use name_group as the canonical index/column label everywhere (RV/RVs/simi rows, scaling index, correlations keys), matching R's row.names/colnames assignment. (2) Expose Xfin and dep as raw np.ndarray (3D) because pandas cannot represent a 3D array; keep the consensus column labels and row index in call so users can slice Xfin[:, :, i] and re-wrap. Optionally add a helper xfin_config(i) -> pd.DataFrame. (3) Put the VMQTE (missing-value / qualitative branch) flag in call so PANOVA's two possible key-sets are self-documenting. (4) Stash random_state and f1ter params (P, tolerance, scale) in call exactly as HCPC stashes its clustering params, since GPA is stochastic. (5) PANOVA defaults to {} and dep to None so a minimal first implementation can omit them while still returning a valid GPAResult (matching the minimal parity set). Do NOT add eig/svd/Block fields.

fixture.dataset_recommendation:
Recommendation: commit a small DETERMINISTIC SYNTHETIC K-configuration CSV (factominer/datasets/data/gpa_synth.csv) as the primary fixture, with wine as an optional secondary if a license-clean wine CSV is ever bundled. Do NOT reshape decathlon/children/tea/poison — none of them naturally form K configurations of the same N objects scored on different variable blocks, so any reshape would be contrived and would NOT match any R data() example (breaking the byte-identical-input guarantee the FAMD stanza established).

DECISIVE REASON — R's GPA is NOT deterministic. Reading the bundled R source at /private/tmp/GPA.R: GPA() calls f1ter(X1, P = 5, ...) (GPA.R:749) which does sample(nbj) for 5 random configuration permutations (GPA.R:588-590), random column permutations and random column sign-flips (GPA.R:596-612), then keeps the best-of-5 restart by a loss criterion. Additionally procrustesbis() uses rnorm() to complete a null-space basis when a configuration block is rank-deficient (GPA.R:289). So the converged consensus/Xfin/scaling depend on R's RNG state. This has two consequences: (1) the R fixture stanza MUST wrap GPA() in set.seed(<fixed>) or the committed JSON drifts on every refresh; (2) the Python port should implement the deterministic CORE (algogpa: iterative orthogonal Procrustes + optional scaling, GPA.R:312-576) as a single pass and skip the stochastic f1ter restart wrapper, so consensus/Xfin can only be compared up to rotation/reflection/sign, never bit-exact.

A synthetic dataset is the right call precisely because we can construct each block to be FULL COLUMN RANK (so procrustesbis never hits the rnorm path) and the only remaining stochasticity is f1ter's permutation search, which set.seed pins. wine, by contrast, has highly collinear sensory blocks that can drive rank-deficiency and amplify run-to-run drift, and it carries the same GPL-flavored provenance burden as the existing CSVs (needs a new PROVENANCE.md + NOTICE.md entry). The synthetic file is GPL-free, byte-stable, and needs only a one-line provenance note ("generated, not derived from FactoMineR").

Concrete construction (reproducible, document the generator in PROVENANCE.md): N=12 objects, K=3 configurations, each configuration = the SAME latent 12x3 object matrix L (drawn once from a fixed seed, e.g. numpy default_rng(0).standard_normal((12,3))) passed through a per-configuration random rotation Q_k (orthogonal 3x3), a positive scale s_k, and a small independent noise term, then written as 9 columns: cfg1 cols v1_1..v1_3, cfg2 cols v2_1..v2_3, cfg3 cols v3_1..v3_3. This guarantees three equal-width (blo[i]=3) full-rank configurations with genuinely high but not identical RV (~0.9), exercising scaling (s_k differ), RV/RVs, simi, and a non-trivial consensus. Use an integer-rounded or 6-decimal-rounded CSV so the committed file is exact.

EXACT GROUP VECTOR: group = c(3, 3, 3) (R) / group=[3,3,3] (Python). All three blocks have equal width, which also satisfies GPA.R:824-836's max(listdimblo)<=1e-5 branch, so res$correlations gains the extra 'averagecor' entry — useful additional coverage.

If wine is bundled later instead: the canonical FactoMineR help example is data(wine); GPA(wine[, -(1:2)], group=c(...)) over the 29 numeric sensory columns (wine is 21x31: col1 Label factor, col2 Soil factor, cols 3:31 numeric). The group vector must sum to the number of selected numeric columns (29 if all kept). Note blocks are unequal width there, so the averagecor branch does NOT fire. Given the determinism concern, prefer synthetic.
fixture.r_fixture_call:
Add to tools/refresh_r_fixtures.R, mirroring the FAMD stanza (read the committed CSV directly so R input is byte-identical to what Python reads), and CRITICALLY wrap in set.seed because GPA's f1ter restart is stochastic. Xfin is a 3D array (N x ncp x K) and is serialized as a LIST OF K matrices (one as.data.frame per slice), keyed by group name — jsonlite cannot serialize a bare 3D array. consensus is 2D (N x ncp). RV/RVs/simi are K x K matrices. scaling is the length-K poids vector. correlations is a named R list of per-block (blo[i] x ncp) matrices (plus 'averagecor' when blocks are equal width).

```r
# ---- GPA on the synthetic K-configuration table ---------------------------
# GPA's internal f1ter() does best-of-5 RANDOM restarts (sample()) and
# procrustesbis() can call rnorm(); pin the seed so the fixture is stable.
dump_gpa <- function(res, group, name.group) {
  K <- length(group)
  # Xfin is a 3D array N x ncp x K -> emit as a list of K data.frames.
  xfin_list <- lapply(seq_len(K), function(k) as.data.frame(res$Xfin[, , k]))
  names(xfin_list) <- name.group
  # correlations is a named list of per-block matrices (+ averagecor).
  cor_list <- lapply(res$correlations, as.data.frame)
  list(
    consensus    = as.data.frame(res$consensus),
    Xfin         = xfin_list,
    RV           = as.data.frame(res$RV),
    RVs          = as.data.frame(res$RVs),
    simi         = as.data.frame(res$simi),
    scaling      = as.numeric(res$scaling),
    correlations = cor_list,
    group        = as.integer(group),
    name_group   = name.group
  )
}

gpa_csv <- file.path(root, "factominer", "datasets", "data", "gpa_synth.csv")
gpa_df  <- read.csv(gpa_csv, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
gpa_group <- c(3, 3, 3)
gpa_names <- paste("group", seq_along(gpa_group), sep = ".")
set.seed(42)
res_gpa <- GPA(gpa_df, group = gpa_group, name.group = gpa_names,
               scale = TRUE, graph = FALSE)
write_json(dump_gpa(res_gpa, gpa_group, gpa_names),
           file.path(out_dir("gpa"), "gpa_synth.json"))
cat("[fixtures] gpa/gpa_synth.json\n")
```

Notes for whoever runs the refresh: (1) verify across two reruns that gpa_synth.json is byte-identical — if not, the seed is not fully controlling f1ter and you must either bump the synthetic blocks to cleanly full-rank or capture multiple seeds. (2) write_json already serializes nested lists/data.frames via jsonlite; the Xfin list-of-frames and correlations list-of-frames round-trip fine. (3) as.data.frame on consensus/Xfin yields jsonlite list-of-objects with the existing _row/rowname row-key handling used by _as_df.
fixture.test_template:
tests/test_gpa.py structure, mirroring test_famd.py / test_mca.py. Two tiers of assertions reflecting that R's GPA is stochastic (f1ter restarts) while RV/RVs/simi are deterministic functions of the RAW input configurations (GPA.R:765-812, computed from Xdd, independent of the random restart):

TIER 1 — rotation/reflection-INVARIANT scalars (rock-solid parity anchors, atol ~1e-7, compared directly, no alignment):
- test_gpa_rv: assert np.allclose(res.RV, r['RV']) — K x K, symmetric, diag handling: R seeds the matrix with -1 then fills i<=j and mirrors, so the diagonal is the self-RV (=1 for full configs); compare full matrix.
- test_gpa_rvs: same for res.RVs vs r['RVs'] (the standardized/adjusted RV).
- test_gpa_simi: same for res.simi vs r['simi'] (similarite(), GPA.R:20-29 — also deterministic for full-rank blocks).
These are the primary acceptance gate: they validate the RV/similarity machinery and the calibre() PCA-prep without any orientation ambiguity.

TIER 2 — consensus / Xfin coordinate blocks (rotation + reflection + per-axis sign ambiguous; Xfin additionally shares the consensus's orientation). Do NOT compare raw coords. Two acceptable approaches, prefer (a):
(a) Compare ROTATION-INVARIANT quantities: pairwise inter-point (inter-object) Euclidean distance matrix of the consensus. dist_py = squareform(pdist(res.consensus)); dist_r = squareform(pdist(r_consensus)); assert np.allclose(dist_py, dist_r, atol=1e-6). Distances are invariant to any orthogonal transform (rotation+reflection) and to axis order, so this sidesteps the entire ambiguity. Do the same per-configuration for each Xfin[k] (its inter-point distances), and assert each configuration's distance matrix matches R's slice. Also assert configuration FIT is preserved: the residual sum-of-squares sum_k ||Xfin_k - consensus||_F^2 should match between Python and R (invariant under a common orthogonal transform applied to all of consensus and every Xfin slice).
(b) If you want to assert coords directly, Procrustes-ALIGN Python to R first: use scipy.spatial.procrustes or an explicit orthogonal Procrustes (R_opt = V @ U.T from SVD of r_consensus.T @ py_consensus, allowing reflection), apply R_opt to BOTH py_consensus and every py Xfin slice (they share one frame), THEN np.allclose with atol ~1e-5. This is the moral equivalent of align_to_reference in _sign.py (test_famd.py / test_mca.py call align_to_reference for sign-only ambiguity); here the ambiguity is full orthogonal, so a Procrustes rotation generalizes that per-axis sign flip. Because the Python port runs a single deterministic algogpa pass (no f1ter restarts), expect a possibly different but equally-valid local optimum — keep atol loose (1e-4..1e-5) and gate strictly only on Tier 1 + the invariant distance/RSS checks.

TIER 2b — scaling: res.scaling vs r['scaling'] is the per-configuration weight vector poids (length K). It is sign/order-stable (R reverses the permutation via order(permutab), GPA.R:751-760) and scale-meaningful, so compare directly with a moderate tolerance (atol 1e-5); if it drifts due to restart selection, downgrade to asserting the RATIO pattern / that all entries are positive and their relative ordering matches.

TIER 2c — correlations: res.correlations is per-block (blo[i] x ncp) correlations of each raw centered block to the consensus (GPA.R:816-837), plus 'averagecor' (equal-width branch fires for group=[3,3,3]). These inherit the consensus's axis orientation, so apply the SAME Procrustes/sign alignment used for the consensus before comparing, or compare |abs| per element with a loose tol. Lowest-priority assertion.

Helpers: reuse a _r_block_to_array-style reader (as in test_famd.py/test_mca.py) for consensus/Xfin frames (handle _row/rowname/X row keys via the conftest _as_df pattern). Add a _gpa() factory: GPA(load_gpa_synth(), group=[3,3,3]). Add a test_gpa_summary_runs smoke test (mirrors test_famd_summary_runs).
